ideas.risks: May fail if no known theorem fits the exact oracle model (only returns binary labels with fixed error), or if constants in that theorem still depend exponentially on inverse-margin/accuracy proxies.
ideas.summary: Do a focused pass over residual-free agnostic boosting literature to find an algorithm that starts from a fixed correlation/advantage oracle and performs only label-to-label calls, then instantiate its assumptions exactly for improper learners. Translate each requirement into the problem’s parameters (query format, runtime, sample, distribution shift) and identify the smallest additional assumption needed.
ideas.title: Search for exact fixed-slack-compatible agnostic booster theorem
ideas.why_promising: If such a theorem already exists, this could close the implication directly without inventing new machinery.

ideas.risks: Constructing the filtered distribution family may be mathematically delicate; the candidate witness can accidentally trivialize via constant predictors or fail to keep source-learner utility on all rounds.
ideas.summary: Build a concrete obstruction where adaptive filtering raises `OPT_C` by conditioning on events defined by past weak hypotheses: choose a class with two complementary submodes of data where low-OPT globally but near-random under residual-driven filters. Show the source guarantee gives no further advantage after a few rounds while any wrapper using this filter class would need super-polynomial sample mass.
ideas.title: Formalize adaptive filter-dirtying counterexample
ideas.why_promising: A single explicit `C,D,F` witness would decisively explain the failure mode and could block broad positive booster strategies.

ideas.risks: Quantifying `SQ` precision can be too coarse without proving that fixed-slab guarantees imply only low-precision correlations; reduction might be nontrivial if oracle outputs are richer than binary predicates.
ideas.summary: Model each fixed-slack improper learner as an SQ algorithm with fixed tolerated correlation gap, then test whether known SQ lower bounds (for agnostic or improper learning) imply that arbitrary-ε refinement requires exponentially finer precision or super-polynomial queries for this class, yielding a conditional negative route.
ideas.title: SQ-precision bottleneck route for hardness
ideas.why_promising: This reframes a semantic gap as a formal precision-to-complexity barrier, which is natural for fixed-advantage oracles.

ideas.risks: The subclass may become too narrow to impact the main open edge if the assumptions are essentially equivalent to already-known strong margin-noise conditions; need to ensure nontrivial and check consistency with distribution-free requirement.
ideas.summary: Define and prove a conditional positive theorem under explicit stability assumptions: bounded filter density ratio, Tsybakov/correct-classification noise, or disagreement-coefficient-type regularity. Show these imply `OPT_C(D_t) <= 1/2-γ_t` with trackable `γ_t` under the wrapper’s reweighting.
ideas.title: Conditional positive theorem under distribution/filter stability
ideas.why_promising: Could produce the first polynomial-time conversion in a natural and clearly checkable regime, and sharpen the boundary between open and false/true cases.

ideas.risks: May require nontrivial derandomization/sampling-theory work to ensure polynomial acceptance while preserving measurable progress; empirical checks may be needed before proof can be closed.
ideas.summary: Replace adaptive rejection-style filtering with a deterministic/oblivious residual forcing sequence based on fixed random partitioning or dyadic bucketing that guarantees polynomial acceptance and bounded drift in `OPT` by construction. Analyze whether such filters admit efficient computable lower bounds on remaining gap.
ideas.title: Non-adaptive or quasi-oblivious filter design
ideas.why_promising: If successful, this bypasses the adaptive filter-drift issue and directly addresses the main blocker identified across all notes.

ideas.risks: Hardness reductions can collapse if the fixed-slack learner is also useful for the reduction target class or if assumptions used are nonstandard/unverifiable.
ideas.summary: Attempt a conditional separation by reducing from a problem where fixed-slack error oracle is equivalent to coarse binary statistics but full ε-agnostic learning is believed hard (e.g., parity/LPN or code classes). Encode the oracle’s outputs to make it easy to satisfy `OPT+β` while showing efficient ε-improvement would imply breaking the source hardness under standard assumptions.
ideas.title: Hardness pipeline via fixed-oracle encoding
ideas.why_promising: A clean reduction would resolve the edge negatively (under standard assumptions) and settle the iteration frontier.
